name: One-Class SVM
analogy: Think of it as stretching a flexible fence around a herd. The fence is pulled as tight as it can go while still keeping nearly all the normal animals inside, and anything that wanders outside the fence is flagged as a stranger.

steps.title: Gather bars that are mostly normal
steps.description: The model is given a set of bars with no labels, on the assumption that most of them are ordinary. It never needs examples of bad bars, only a good picture of what usual looks like.
steps.inExample: It is given 20,000 5-minute MNQ bars, each described by four features, scaled to comparable sizes.

steps.title: Rescale the features
steps.description: The model is sensitive to feature size, so every feature is put on the same scale first. Without this, a feature measured in large numbers would dominate the boundary.
steps.inExample: Return, range ratio, volume ratio and distance from average are each rescaled to have an average of zero and a typical size of one.

steps.title: Choose how curved the fence may be
steps.description: A kernel setting lets the boundary bend around oddly shaped groups of normal bars instead of being a flat cut. A looser setting gives a smoother fence and a tighter one wraps closely around the data.
steps.inExample: A smooth bell-shaped kernel is chosen so the fence can curve around the main cluster and a smaller side cluster of opening-hour bars.

steps.title: Say how many bars may fall outside
steps.description: You set an upper limit on the share of training bars allowed outside the fence. It acts as a dial between a tight fence that rejects many bars and a loose one that accepts nearly everything.
steps.inExample: The share is set to 2 percent, so about 400 of the 20,000 training bars may end up outside.

steps.title: Fit the tightest fence that fits
steps.description: The model finds the boundary that encloses most of the normal bars while keeping the enclosed region as small as possible. Only a few of the bars, the ones sitting on or beyond the boundary, end up defining it.
steps.inExample: The fit keeps about 410 boundary-defining bars, called support bars, and discards the rest from the final rule.

steps.title: Score a new bar by its side of the fence
steps.description: A new bar gets a signed score: positive if it falls inside the fence, negative if outside, and the farther from the fence the larger the number. A plain inside or outside label comes from the sign.
steps.inExample: The new bar scores minus 3 on the model's own scale, which puts it outside the fence.

steps.title: Act on the label or the score
steps.description: The yes-or-no label is enough for a simple flag, but the score lets you rank bars from slightly odd to very odd. A stricter threshold can be set on the score if the default flags too much.
steps.inExample: A threshold of minus 1 is used to flag only strongly unusual bars, and this bar passes that threshold.

useFor.example: Learning the shape of ordinary 5-minute bars on MNQ so that any bar outside it triggers a closer look.
Checking that today's feature row resembles the data a model was trained on, and pausing the model if it falls outside.
Watching the share of bars outside the fence climb over several days, which suggests the market is behaving differently from the training period.
Removing the roughly 2 percent of bars outside the fence before fitting a forecasting model.

avoidWhen: You have hundreds of thousands of bars; training slows steeply as bars are added, so an isolation forest is the more practical choice.
The training bars contain many anomalies already; the fence will stretch to include them and stop flagging that kind of bar.

example.scenario: A 5-minute MNQ bar closes. A One-Class SVM trained on a year of ordinary bars is asked whether this bar lies inside the region of normal behaviour.

input.summary: Four rescaled features describing the bar that just closed.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the 5-minute bar closed, shown for reference and not used as a feature.

fields.name: return over the bar
fields.value: down about a third of a percent
fields.meaning: How far price fell during this bar, a large move for a 5-minute bar.

fields.name: range against average true range
fields.meaning: The bar's range was nearly three times the typical recent range.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: Trading was much heavier than normal.

fields.name: distance from the 50-bar average
fields.meaning: How far the close sits below its recent average price.

output.summary: A signed score and an inside-or-outside label.

fields.name: decision score
fields.meaning: Negative means outside the fence of normal behaviour; larger negative values mean farther outside. The scale is the model's own.

fields.name: label
fields.meaning: The bar is not inside the region that the model learned as normal.

fields.name: share of training bars allowed outside
fields.meaning: The dial that sets how tight the fence was drawn.

example.reading: A large drop with wide range and heavy volume sits outside the learned fence, so the model calls it unusual. That is not a prediction of what comes next: use it to widen risk limits, pause a model trained only on calm data, or mark the bar for review.
